meta.title: Medieval World
meta.subtitle: Pilot: Byzantium, the Caliphate, the Holy Roman Empire, the Mongols, Mali and China, 650–1500
meta.description: Realms, empires and peoples from 650 to 1500: dynasties as phases, unions and empires as their own rows, and which empire each realm was part of when.
meta.credits: Dates from Wikipedia articles, read from the English Wikipedia dump of 1 November 2026; each date cites its infobox field, section or lead sentence.

events.title: Africa lost to the Umayyads
events.descr: The Umayyad Caliphate completes its conquest of North Africa; the empire then stabilises under the Isaurian dynasty.

sources.sourceLocation: lead: "In 698, Africa was lost to the Umayyad Caliphate, but the empire stabilised under the Isaurian dynasty."
infobox event3: Conquest of North Africa, 698

events.title: Sack of Constantinople (Fourth Crusade)
events.descr: The Fourth Crusade sacks Constantinople; the empire splits into competing Greek rump states and Latin realms.

events.title: Constantinople recovered
events.descr: The Empire of Nicaea recaptures Constantinople and restores the empire, which holds only regional power from then on.

sources.sourceLocation: lead: "Despite the eventual recovery of Constantinople in 1261, the reconstituted empire wielded only regional power during its final two centuries."

events.title: Fall of Constantinople
events.descr: The Ottomans take Constantinople, ending the empire.

sources.sourceLocation: lead: "The fall of Constantinople to the Ottomans in 1453 brought the empire to an end."

events.title: Charlemagne crowned emperor
events.descr: Pope Leo III crowns the Frankish king Charlemagne as Roman Emperor on 25 December 800, reviving the title in the West.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event_pre: Charlemagne crowned Emperor, 25 December 800

events.title: Otto I crowned emperor
events.descr: The title, lapsed by 924, is revived when Pope John XII crowns Otto of Saxony on 2 February 962.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event_start: Otto I crowned Emperor, 2 February 962
lead: "The title had again lapsed by 924 but was revived again in 962 with the crowning of Otto of Saxony as emperor by Pope John XII."

events.title: Burgundy joins the empire
events.descr: Conrad II incorporates the Kingdom of Burgundy, the third of the empire's constituent kingdoms.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event1: Conrad II incorporates the Kingdom of Burgundy, 2 February 1033

events.title: Golden Bull of 1356
events.descr: The Golden Bull is issued in 1356.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event2: Golden Bull of 1356, 10 January and 25 December 1356

events.title: Conquest of Persia
events.descr: The Rashidun Caliphate conquers the Sasanian Empire; the conquest is completed under Uthman in 651.

lead: "His reign oversaw the completion of the conquest of Persia in 651 and continued the military campaigns into Byzantine territories."

events.title: Ali assassinated; Mu'awiya becomes caliph
events.descr: A Kharijite dissident kills Ali; Mu'awiya, the governor of Syria, wins the First Fitna and founds the Umayyad Caliphate.

events.title: Abd al-Malik wins the Second Fitna
events.descr: Abd al-Malik restores Umayyad control over the Caliphate after defeating the Zubayrids.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event2: Abd al-Malik wins the Second Fitna, 692
lead: "His eldest son and successor Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan restored Umayyad control over the Caliphate after defeating the Zubayrids in 692."

events.title: Abbasid Revolution
events.descr: The Abbasids overthrow Caliph Marwan II, and most of the Umayyad family are slain.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event_end: Abbasid revolution, 750
lead: "In 750, the Abbasids overthrew Caliph Marwan II, and most of the Umayyad family were slain."

events.title: Founding of Baghdad
events.descr: The second Abbasid caliph, al-Mansur, founds Baghdad and makes it the capital.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event1: Founding of Baghdad, 762
lead: "The Abbasids first centered their government in Kufa, Iraq, but in 762 the second caliph al-Mansur founded the city of Baghdad and made it the capital."

events.title: Buyids take control of Baghdad
events.descr: The caliphs become figureheads; real power rests with the Iranian Buyids.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event5: Buyids take control of Baghdad, 945
infobox event6: The Seljuks conquer Baghdad, 1055

events.title: Mongol siege of Baghdad
events.descr: The Mongols under Hulagu Khan sack Baghdad and execute Caliph al-Musta'sim, the effective end of the Abbasid Caliphate.

events.title: Abbasid caliphs re-established in Cairo
events.descr: The Mamluk sultans reinstate a surviving branch of the dynasty in Cairo, without political power.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event9: Abbasids re-established as ceremonial caliphs in Cairo, 1261
lead: "A surviving branch of the Abbasid dynasty was formally reinstated in 1261 by the Mamluk sultans in Cairo, but it lacked any political power."

events.descr: Kublai Khan proclaims the dynastic name "Great Yuan" and claims the succession of former Chinese dynasties.

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event_start: Kublai's proclamation of the dynastic name "Great Yuan", 5 November 1271
lead: "His younger brother Kublai Khan was proclaimed the new Great Khan and in 1271 founded the Yuan dynasty."

sources.sourceLocation: infobox event_end: Sack of Sarai by the Crimean Khanate, 1502

events.title: Conquest of Sosso
events.descr: The conquest of Sosso marks the emergence of Mali as a major power, with the Kouroukan Fouga as its constitution.

events.title: Sakura's coup
events.descr: Sakura, a former slave of the imperial family risen to general, seizes power.

sources.sourceLocation: lead: "In 1285, Sakura, a former slave of the imperial family who had risen to the rank of general, carried out a military coup."

events.title: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage to Mecca
events.descr: His gifts and spending of gold cause significant inflation in Egypt.

sources.sourceLocation: lead: "He made a famous pilgrimage to Mecca from 1324 to 1326, where his generous gifts and his expenditure of gold caused significant inflation in Egypt."

events.title: Wu Zetian proclaims the Zhou dynasty
events.descr: Wu Zhao takes the throne from her son, Emperor Ruizong of Tang, the only legitimate Chinese female emperor.

lead: "The dynasty consisted of the reign of one female emperor, Wu Zhao (Wu Zetian), who usurped the throne of her son, the Emperor Ruizong of Tang, in 690."

events.title: Shenlong Coup restores the Tang
events.descr: Emperor Zhongzong of Tang is restored to the throne.
